mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP indicates a growing economy, which leads to higher consumer spending and increased demand for goods and services, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during periods of strong GDP growth (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate below 0.1% signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing and spending, and ultimately positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, which leads to increased consumer confidence and spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative during periods of low unemployment (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates increased economic activity, which leads to higher demand for goods and services, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during periods of high industrial production (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts and a decrease in unemployment rate indicate a strong economy, which leads to increased consumer spending and demand for goods and services, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate and an increase in GDP indicate an accommodative monetary policy and a growing economy, which leads to increased borrowing and spending, and ultimately positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A high payroll employment level indicates a strong labor market, which leads to increased consumer confidence and spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index and an increase in retail sales indicate decreased inflationary pressures and increased consumer spending, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in low-inflation periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
